outcomes.text: Understand short recordings about everyday needs, such as shopping, directions and instructions.
Understand factual information and ideas in announcements, messages, news, interviews and dialogues about familiar topics.
Understand descriptions of events, opinions, emotions, hopes and ambitions in simple spoken texts.
Identify main points, specific information and details in recordings about everyday subjects.
Recognise main points, themes, opinions, ideas, emotions and attitudes in predictable spoken texts.
Infer the meaning of occasional unfamiliar words and expressions from listening context.
Understand short, simple texts such as public signs, notices and transport information.
Understand authentic texts about familiar topics, including articles, emails, blogs and letters.
Understand descriptions of events, opinions, emotions, hopes and ambitions in simple written texts.
Identify main points, specific information and details in predictable texts such as advertisements, menus and timetables.
Recognise main points, themes, opinions, ideas, emotions and attitudes in predictable written texts.
Infer the meaning of occasional unfamiliar words and expressions from reading context.
Take part in brief social exchanges and communicate about familiar topics to meet basic needs.
Participate in spontaneous conversations about personal interests and everyday life.
Describe past events and experiences, express hopes and ambitions, and briefly justify opinions and plans.
Communicate with reasonable accuracy using varied structures, tenses and relevant vocabulary.
Link shorter points into a connected sequence using simple conjunctions and connectors.
Use suitable strategies to keep conversations going.
Use pronunciation and intonation features to express meaning and attitude.
Complete forms with simple personal details.
Write simple factual information using everyday vocabulary and expressions.
Write linked simple phrases and sentences about personal life, surroundings and everyday topics.
Write connected texts about familiar subjects, including plans, preferences, family, education, work and travel.
Describe past events and experiences, opinions, hopes and ambitions, giving brief reasons.
Communicate with reasonable accuracy using varied structures, time frames and relevant vocabulary.
Connect shorter written elements into a coherent sequence using simple linking words.
Use definite, indefinite and partitive articles, including de after negative verb forms.
Use French nouns with correct gender and singular or plural forms.
Use adjective agreement, possessive, demonstrative, interrogative, indefinite, comparative and superlative forms.
Use adverbs of time, place, questioning, manner, possibility, frequency, quantity, comparison and intensity.
Use personal, reflexive, object, demonstrative, interrogative, relative, disjunctive, possessive and indefinite pronouns.
Use regular, irregular and reflexive verbs in appropriate persons, forms, moods, voices and tenses.
Use coordinating and subordinating conjunctions to connect ideas.
Use prepositions expressing place, time, movement and other relationships.
Use cardinal and ordinal numbers.
Express quantity using terms such as enough, much, half, little, several, too much and so much.
Express dates, clock times, years and other time references, including the 24-hour clock.
Understand and use common French adjectives describing qualities, appearance, conditions, opinions and comparisons.
Understand and use common adverbs and prepositions for place, possibility, frequency, manner, intensity and quantity.
Understand and use cardinal numbers from zero to one million.
Understand and use ordinal numbers, including first, second, third and subsequent forms.
Understand and use vocabulary for halves, thirds and quarters.
Understand and use common vocabulary for approximation, quantity, comparison, majority, minority, totals and frequency.
Understand and use common verbs for everyday actions, communication, feelings, movement, thought, organisation and interaction.
Understand and use vocabulary for everyday activities and routines.
Understand and use common expressions referring to sequence, duration, frequency, past, present and future time.
Understand and express clock times, parts of the day, durations and units of time.
Understand and use the French names of the days of the week and weekend.
